title: Deep space photos
examples: How far away are the galaxies in a deep field picture?
What is the difference between Hubble and James Webb images?
Can we see things that are older than Earth?

explain.say: Today we look at amazing deep space photos. These pictures show us very distant parts of space. We are looking at deep fields today.
The Hubble telescope took some famous deep field images. These images let us see thousands of galaxies. They are like looking into the past.
The James Webb Space Telescope sees things differently. It is great at seeing infrared light. This helps see through dust clouds.
These deep fields show us thousands of galaxies. Each galaxy is a huge group of stars. They are spread across vast distances.
In real life, looking at a deep field is like looking through a time machine. You see galaxies as they were long ago.
A common mistake is thinking all galaxies look the same. In fact, they come in many different shapes. Some are spiral, some are elliptical.

faq.q: What is the main difference between Hubble and Webb?
faq.a: Hubble primarily sees visible light, while Webb specializes in infrared light. This allows Webb to see through cosmic dust clouds much better.
asks: What is the main advantage of JWST?

faq.q: How far away are these galaxies?
faq.a: The galaxies seen are incredibly distant, meaning the light we see left them billions of years ago. This makes them look like windows into the early universe.
asks: Can we see the beginning of time?
How old is the light in these photos?

faq.q: What is a deep field image?
faq.a: A deep field image is a very long exposure photograph of a small patch of sky. Because it is so long, it captures light from countless galaxies spread over huge distances.
asks: What does 'deep field' mean in astronomy?
Is it just a picture of a galaxy?

faq.q: Do all galaxies look like spirals?
faq.a: No, galaxies come in many shapes. You can see spiral shapes, like our Milky Way, and smooth elliptical shapes. They are very diverse.
asks: Are there different types of galaxies?

faq.a: Infrared light passes through dust clouds that block visible light. This lets astronomers see stars and galaxies hidden behind the cosmic dust.
asks: How does Webb see through dust?

facts: Deep field images capture light from many galaxies.
The James Webb Space Telescope observes in infrared light.
Galaxies are massive systems containing billions of stars.
The light from these galaxies traveled for billions of years to reach us.

quiz.say: Which telescope is known for observing in infrared light?
quiz.why: The James Webb Space Telescope is specifically designed to observe in infrared light, which helps see through dust.

wrong.1: Hubble is excellent, but its primary focus is visible light, not deep infrared.
wrong.2: The Moon is a natural satellite and does not take deep space photos.
wrong.3: Earth's atmosphere blocks much of the infrared light needed for deep views.

quiz.say: What does a deep field image show us?
quiz.why: A deep field collects light over a long time from a small patch, revealing thousands of galaxies.

wrong.1: Deep fields show vast areas, not just one star system.
wrong.2: The images look billions of years into the past, far beyond our solar system.
wrong.3: While it shows galaxies, it covers a much wider, deeper area of space.
